correctness.rationale: Exact integral GL(2,Z) conjugacy produces S(u,v)=(u+δ,4v+u+f). The explicit n-th iterate has H_n=(4^n−1)/3 and integer W_n=(4^n−1−3n)/9. The periodic base congruence imposes q|n; the one-dimensional kernel character (H_n,L_n) has gcd H_n and hence precisely H_n embedded essential circle components, all with primitive winding (3,−1) in skew coordinates and (1,−1) in the original torus. Parallel character fibers prove whole-component least periods and validate Möbius inversion. Derivative eigenvalues 1 and 4^n establish neutral-tangent and expanding-normal splitting. Fourier frequencies transform b→4b; unit Koopman eigenfunctions have b=0, establishing full eigenvalue group, ergodicity criterion and rational invariant field. Standard Lebesgue ergodicity of expanding circles and the pointwise ergodic theorem give respective Haar-typical orbit-closure dimensions one and two. Exact rational code was run on six translation cases (q=1,2,3,7,10) but is not the proof of any infinite statement.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader results on period sets describe existence of some period for unshifted linear endomorphisms, not exact counts and topology of all connected periodic components for real translations. Rational-lattice periodic orbit results count finite rational grid points; the present objects are full essential circles. General ergodic skew-product methods supply ingredients but no inspected theorem jointly implies the precise B(q,k) formula and 1/2 Hausdorff orbit-closure transition for this model.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The 2018 paper proves fixed-point absence for its nonzero rotation displacement and computes eigenvalues 1 and 4; neither entails absence of all higher periods for irrational displacement or exact rational period-component counts. The 2015 period-set paper proves that the unshifted linear map has every positive period; this cannot imply the shifted example has only multiples of q, nor that exact components equal (1/3)∑μ(k/d)(4^(qd)-1). Combined with standard rotation and expanding-circle facts, the result is freshly derived here, without claiming the constituent facts are new.

originality.rationale: The complete original 2018 model article and the full 2015 linear toral period-set preprint were read and statements compared, including the latter’s period-set Table 2 for eigenvalues (1,4). The source supplies fixed-point and Lyapunov analyses but not the combined translation-arithmetic circle census and almost-everywhere orbit closures; the 2015 paper classifies linear period sets rather than affine-translation-dependent component counts. Semantic research-index searches and accessible prior claims yielded no equivalent or dominating specific theorem. General standard arguments are acknowledged, and missing full texts of related background works remain risks, so priority is not asserted as established universally.
residual_risks: A previously unnoticed general affine-toral skew-product theorem might give the same arithmetic component census or spectral-orbit closure characterization.

value.rationale: The published map is a natural degree-four torus system with a neutral eigendirection and positive transverse Lyapunov exponent; its numerically plotted behavior makes the full distribution of recurrent orbits and their supports mathematically important. An exact, complete primitive-period component-count formula for every translation and the sharp arithmetic jump of generic orbit-closure dimension from 1 to 2 are intrinsic global invariants not given by a fixed-point discussion, Lyapunov spectrum, or a generic textbook rotation exercise. The reported 349525 ten-period circles and ten typical support circles in the original experimental parameters give an exact benchmark; the result is not claimed to imply cryptographic strength or new general ergodic theory.
